clue.text: Shamed and criticised after article

indicators.note: after places the criticism word behind the article in the answer

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
bashed means attacked verbally, harshly criticised

explanation.surface: Someone publicly humiliated and attacked in print after a newspaper article about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' reads as a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article A; 'after' puts BASHED behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone embarrassed and made to feel ashamed is abashed.

clue.text: Early strains ordered to be planted in Australia

indicators.note: planted in means set inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, ordered

explanation.surface: Seeds of early plant strains ordered to be grown in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strains' suggests plant varieties but means tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a piece of music or poem for dawn, so these are morning songs.

clue.text: Sales promoter confusing and taking in mother

indicators.note: taking in means holding the mother word inside
confusing means jumbling the letters

parts.note: ma is mother

explanation.surface: A salesman muddled and drew his mother into the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated answer is informal; 'confusing' gives ADN, an anagram of the plain word 'and', and 'taking in' wraps it round mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertising man creates advertisements that promote sales.

clue.text: Edges of the door cracked, beset by spell against religious standards

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by the spell word

parts.note: a hex is a spell or curse

indicators.note: edges means the first and last letters of the word
cracked means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cursed, splintered door defying the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges of' works on 'the' alone; 'cracked' scrambles door to RODO; 'beset by' means the curse sits on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodox views depart from accepted doctrine, so are unorthodox.

clue.text: Daughter broke up? Show sadness

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: broke means having no money, poor

explanation.surface: A daughter cracked; did she display her grief?
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke up' looks like a verb but is POOR reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to droop is to sag or flag, as dejected people do.

clue.text: Single rule should restrict nonsense, theoretically

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the first pieces close round the nonsense word

parts.note: single means one
pap is worthless or trivial matter, nonsense

explanation.surface: A lone regulation ought in principle to curb silly talk.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE and R together surround PAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something true in principle but perhaps not in practice holds only as written down.

clue.text: Noticing old book with Jeeves, say

parts.note: Jeeves is P G Wodehouse's valet, an example of a household servant

explanation.surface: Spotting an old volume featuring the fictional valet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an observant person is quick to notice things.

clue.text: Cracked receptacle for liquid?

definitions.meaning: cracked in the informal sense means crazy, mad
a child's chamber pot is a receptacle for urine

explanation.surface: A broken container for liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' suggests a damaged pot but means crazy; the question mark flags the coy liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is informal for crazy; the other is a small chamber pot for children.

clue.text: Excusing fellow getting hooked by edge of nail

indicators.note: hooked by means caught inside the nail word

parts.note: a nail paring is a clipped edge of a fingernail
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Letting off a man who snagged himself on a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' looks like any man but is an Oxbridge college fellow; 'getting hooked by' puts him inside the clipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pardoning someone means forgiving or excusing them.

clue.text: Responses concerning kids assimilating only one-third of basic knowledge

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: assimilating means absorbing the letter inside the children word

parts.note: tots are small children
basic knowledge is the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, so one third is a single R

explanation.surface: Answers about children who have learnt only a little basic education.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; one of them gives R inside TOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: retorts are sharp replies.

clue.text: What we think of as collision will involve one unduly pushy

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the phrase closes round the numeral

parts.words: What we think of as collision
parts.note: from our point of view a collision is a bump to us, i.e. something knocking into us
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A collision seen from our side involving someone over-assertive.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase is read whimsically: a collision, to us, is a 'bump to us'; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone self-assertive and over-confident to the point of being offensive is bumptious.

clue.text: It involves many a card sharp, while bringing in nothing

indicators.note: bringing in means taking a letter inside the flavour word

parts.note: sharp in taste means tart
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A card sharp's game involving lots of cards, played while risking nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card sharp' reads as a cheat, but 'card' belongs to the definition and 'sharp' is the flavour TART.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot pack is a deck of seventy-eight cards used in fortune-telling and some games.

clue.text: US soldier leaving less attractive US restaurant

indicators.note: the soldier leaving means his letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: dingier means drabber, less attractive
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier walks out of a shabby American eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is a cheap roadside eating place in North America, a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Who'll show some energy in wild orgy?

definitions.text: Who'll show some energy in wild orgy?

indicators.note: in places the energy symbol inside the shuffled letters

parts.note: some, as in a portion of something, means part

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running riot into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Who would display a bit of vigour at an unrestrained orgy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' is a pronoun meaning a portion; 'wild' mixes it with orgy to PARTYGOR and 'in' slips the energy symbol inside, while the whole clue describes the reveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending a wild party would be expected to show some vigour there.

clue.text: Woods in an awful part of Wales

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some woods in a dreadful corner of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges WOODSINAN. Snowdonia is a mountainous region of north-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the mountainous north-west region around Snowdon is a well-known area of Wales.

clue.text: Love to remain at hospital, receiving ultimate in care from medic

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: receiving means taking a letter inside the remain word

parts.note: to stop at a place is to remain there

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sweetheart stays in hospital, getting the best care from a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate in care' is E, received into STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath is a practitioner treating bones and muscles by manipulation, a kind of healer.

clue.text: Required Queen to carry various cases when entering US city

indicators.note: entering means going inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: carrying means holding the shuffled letters inside

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: various means differing, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: The Queen had to carry assorted luggage on arrival in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like luggage but is just letters: 'various' makes CESSA, 'to carry' puts it inside the monarch, and 'when entering' sends all that into the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something needed or essential is necessary.

clue.text: Change of heart in what bishop may do, leading to paradise

indicators.note: changing the heart means altering the middle letter of the word

parts.note: a bishop may bless a congregation

explanation.surface: A bishop's blessing that changes someone's heart and leads them to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' sounds spiritual but swaps the central E of BLESS for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perfect happiness, heaven on earth.

clue.text: Stage performer in Globe elevated an expression of passion

parts.note: a globe is a sphere, a ball

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: An actor at the Globe theatre raised a passionate cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Globe' suggests Shakespeare's theatre but is BALL; AN IRE read upwards is ERINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ballet dancer performs on stage.

clue.text: Treatment for addiction leads to extreme tension during party times

indicators.note: during means the letters sit inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the following two words

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Rehab follows extreme stress over party season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' looks like seasons but is the multiplication sign; 'leads to' takes the heads of extreme tension, which go 'during' the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A detoxification programme rids the body of drugs or alcohol, treating addiction.

clue.text: Ambassador relinquishing last award

indicators.note: relinquishing its last letter means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an ambassador is a diplomat

explanation.surface: An envoy gives up a final prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded for completing a course of study.

clue.text: Captain initially confused, neglecting ship, to hazard ignoring ship's list

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word
neglecting means leaving out the ship letters

parts.note: at a loss means bewildered, confused
SS is steamship

indicators.note: ignoring means dropping the ship letters from the word

parts.note: to hazard a guess is to guess
SS again is steamship

explanation.surface: A bewildered captain leaves his vessel and guesses wildly, ignoring the ship's manifest.
explanation.walkthrough: AT A LOSS loses SS to give ATALO and GUESS loses SS to give GUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a catalogue is a systematic itemised record.

clue.text: Holding unconventional opinions, discharged from Engineers? About time

indicators.note: about means going around the time letter

parts.note: ex-REME, a former member of the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers

explanation.surface: A former army engineer with radical views, released at last.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps; ex-REME goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme views are radical, far from the mainstream.

clue.text: Old magistrate's opposing views seriously upset lawyer, initially

parts.note: pro and con are views for and against

indicators.note: initially here takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A former judge's conflicting opinions badly upset a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' applies to all three words seriously upset lawyer, giving SUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A proconsul was a governor of a Roman province, an official of ancient times.

clue.text: Different parent blowing top

indicators.note: blowing its top means losing the first letter in a down clue

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A distinctly unusual parent loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' suggests an angry outburst but removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something distinct or alternative.

clue.text: Runs banks, ousting leader

indicators.note: ousting the leader means dropping the first letter

parts.note: banks are slopes

explanation.surface: A financial run on the banks topples their chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' and 'banks' suggest finance but mean striding and slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lope is to run with long, easy strides.

clue.text: Overseas resident's vote included in record, after reflection

indicators.note: reflection, as in a mirror, means the result is read backwards
included in means the ballot mark goes inside the recording word

parts.note: a tape is a recording
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: An expatriate's ballot recorded after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes in TAPE to give TAPXE, then 'after reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: an expatriate is someone living abroad.

clue.text: What sounds like excellent work on the pipes

indicators.note: sounds like signals a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: plum describes something excellent and desirable, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: A first-rate job installing pipes, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to install or repair pipes as a plumber does.

clue.text: Significant order taken by a good hotel in Northern Irish town

parts.note: the OM, Order of Merit, is a prestigious British honour
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An important booking accepted by a fine hotel in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a booking but is the Order of Merit, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Range shown in measure of current dilute fluid

parts.note: the amp is the unit of electric current

indicators.note: fluid means flowing, changeable, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: A scientist's range of readings in a weak solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilute fluid' reads as a watered-down liquid, but 'fluid' is the anagram signal, making LITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: amplitude means breadth or extent, the scope of something.

clue.text: Wandering round Centre for Archery, where you'll see butts

indicators.note: round means the wandering word goes around the letter

parts.note: astray means wandering off course

indicators.note: centre means the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: Arrows going off course around an archery centre, where targets are set up.
explanation.walkthrough: Archery butts are target mounds; here 'butts' are cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette ends, called butts, are stubbed out in an ashtray.

clue.text: Assumed University rep will ignore University and take awkward steps

parts.note: an assumed manner is a sham, a pretence

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the abbreviation from the word

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A fake student representative skips the college and stumbles about.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson; BLUE loses U to give BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to shamble is to walk clumsily and awkwardly.
